note: These proverbial phrases sit on Wikipedia's list with no author named — pure anonymous folk wisdom, as far as that page is concerned. But each one has a well-documented origin as somebody's specific written line. The wording wore down into a proverb; the paper trail didn't disappear, it just stopped getting cited.

pairs.proverb: Knowledge is power, guard it well
pairs.aphorism: Ipsa scientia potestas est — knowledge itself is power.
pairs.author: widely credited to Francis Bacon

pairs.proverb: Well done is better than well said
pairs.aphorism: Well done is better than well said.
pairs.author: commonly attributed to Benjamin Franklin

pairs.proverb: What does not kill me makes me stronger
pairs.aphorism: Was mich nicht umbringt, macht mich stärker.
pairs.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

pairs.proverb: Whom the Gods love die young
pairs.aphorism: Ὃν οἱ θεοὶ φιλοῦσιν ἀποθνῄσκει νέος — he whom the gods love dies young.
pairs.author: Menander

pairs.proverb: A friend to everyone is a friend to no one
pairs.aphorism: He who has many friends has no friend.
pairs.author: often traced to Aristotle
pairs.source: a later compression of the friendship discussion in the Nicomachean Ethics

pairs.proverb: The pen is mightier than the sword
pairs.aphorism: The pen is mightier than the sword.
pairs.author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton

pairs.proverb: Discretion is the better part of valour
pairs.aphorism: The better part of valour is discretion.
pairs.author: William Shakespeare

pairs.proverb: Youth is wasted on the young
pairs.aphorism: Youth is wasted on the young.
pairs.author: often attributed to George Bernard Shaw
pairs.source: no verified source has ever turned up — a coinage floating without a paper trail, misattributed with real confidence for over a century
